criteria.evidence: No `strategy.matrix` anywhere; the workflow hard-codes three separate jobs (nightly-e2e-linux/macos/windows) with duplicated steps, despite the user asking for a matrix over OS.
Windows job: `irm https://entire.sh/install.ps1 | iex` written as if the script existed.
All jobs use actions/checkout with `ref: main`.

Loops `mise run test:e2e --agent "$agent" "$test_name"` over 7 agents, but gemini-cli (present in the install case statement and GEMINI_API_KEY env, and a documented agent in e2e.yml) is silently omitted from the agent list with no stated reason; only roger-roger's Windows exclusion has a reason.
Single test TestMidTurnCommit_DifferentFilesThanPreviousTurn selected, described as 2 prompts, commits and checkpoint validation.
Turn 0: 'let me look at a few E2E tests... check checkpoint-related tests' and read existing_files_test before choosing.
Turn 0 summarized e2e.yml, e2e-windows.yml, nightly.yml, release.yml before proposing the plan.
Each OS job runs a single step looping `for agent in "${agents[@]}"` sequentially; no per-agent matrix.
Commit 5015de17 on branch add-nightly-matrix-e2e-test; push attempted, then told user 'the test environment doesn't have network access to push'.

judge.reason: The replay delivers a nightly workflow with the correct per-OS install methods, main checkout, one smoke test and sequential per-agent runs, and it committed locally and reported the push failure. It fails because it uses three hand-duplicated jobs rather than an OS matrix as explicitly requested, and it leaves gemini-cli out of the agent list without any stated reason.
